title: Surface-Selective Probe of Spin-Triplet Superconductivity in Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Kilian Krötzsch, Zekang Zhou, Kryštof Kolář, Yonggen Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Moty Heiblum, Cyprian Lewandowski, Mitali Banerjee
abstract: Superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene has been observed across many layer numbers, with mounting evidence pointing toward spin-triplet pairing, yet complementary probes of the superconducting spin structure remain needed. Here we use one-sided WS$_2$ proximity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene (R5G) as a surface-selective spin-orbit probe. The induced Ising spin-orbit coupling is strongest for carriers localized near the WS$_2$ interface, allowing the displacement field to tune the overlap between superconducting carriers and the spin-orbit perturbation. We observe a strongly asymmetric superconducting landscape: two robust pockets, SC1 and SC2, survive only on mutually opposite signs of displacement field, while a third pocket, SC3, is substantially weaker. Gate-tracking features, quantum oscillations, and self-consistent band-structure calculations identify the layer polarization and Fermi-surface character of the relevant carriers. The robust superconducting states are absent or strongly weakened when the active high-DOS carriers are polarized toward the WS$_2$ interface. Since Ising spin-orbit coupling is compatible with time-reversed spin-singlet pairing but competes with same-spin intervalley triplet pairing by canting or pinning the parent spin texture, this surface-selective suppression provides additional evidence for spin-triplet superconductivity involving both hole-like and electron-like carriers. Our results establish one-sided TMD proximity as a displacement-field-tunable probe of superconducting spin structure in rhombohedral graphene.
summary: This research uses surface-selective measurements on graphene proximitized by WS2 to investigate the spin structure of superconductivity. By observing how superconducting pockets appear or disappear depending on carrier polarization relative to the interface, the authors provide strong evidence supporting a spin-triplet pairing mechanism. The combination of advanced transport measurements and theoretical modeling makes this a powerful tool for studying correlated electron phenomena in 2D materials.
main_problem: To obtain complementary probes of the superconducting spin structure in rhombohedral graphene, as direct magnetic field probing is challenging due to multiple possible microscopic mechanisms for field-robust superconductivity.
main_result: The surface-selective proximity coupling to WS2 acts as a displacement-field-tunable probe, providing evidence for spin-triplet superconductivity by observing superconducting asymmetry dependent on carrier polarization relative to the interface.
method: The study combines low-temperature magnetotransport measurements (measuring $R_{xx}$ and differential resistance) with theoretical self-consistent band structure calculations using a mean-field Hartree-Fock approach.
model_or_system: The system is rhombohedral pentalayer graphene (R5G) proximitized on one side by WS2. The physics involves analyzing the interplay between superconducting pairing, induced Ising spin-orbit coupling (SOC), and carrier polarization across different electronic regimes (bulk vs. surface pockets).
key_observables: Superconducting pocket robustness ($	ext{SC1}, 	ext{SC2}, 	ext{SC3}$), asymmetry in superconductivity under displacement field reversal, quantum oscillation patterns, and Fermi-surface topology.
important_parameters: Low temperature ($T \simeq 8.5 	ext{ mK}$), zero magnetic field ($	ext{B}=0 	ext{ T}$), and the magnitude of the displacement field ($D/\epsilon_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed asymmetry is due to the surface-selective nature of the Ising SOC, which competes with different pairing symmetries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate longitudinal resistance vs. carrier density and displacement field, quantum oscillation patterns in gate voltage planes, and schematics detailing the three distinct superconducting pockets ($	ext{SC1}-	ext{SC3}$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the experimental platform using magnetotransport measurements to map out superconducting regimes based on external fields. It then uses quantum oscillations and band structure calculations to characterize the underlying electronic topology (Fermi surface). Finally, it integrates these findings by analyzing how the SOC modifies the pairing state, leading to the conclusion about spin-triplet superconductivity.
why_interesting: The work provides a highly tunable platform for probing exotic superconducting symmetries in 2D materials. The use of proximity coupling as a 'spin probe' is valuable because it allows researchers to selectively perturb and measure specific components of the pairing order parameter, which is crucial for understanding unconventional superconductivity mechanisms.
